This script follows the four practicals of the full-day course in order. Run it from a project folder that contains the `data` folder from the course download. Each section matches a chapter of the course website, [cambiotraining.github.io/visual-data-communication](https://cambiotraining.github.io/visual-data-communication/), where you will find more explanation and the exercises.

# Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)

penguins <- read_csv("data/penguins.csv")
finches <- read_csv("data/finches.csv")
gapminder <- read_csv("data/gapminder_2010.csv")
gap_years <- read_csv("data/gapminder_1960_2010.csv")

# a folder for saved figures
dir.create("figures", showWarnings = FALSE)
```

# Practical 1: building a plot in layers

Website chapter 1, *Building a plot in layers*.

## Layer 1: data and aesthetics

The first layer says which data to use and which variables go on which axis. Nothing is drawn yet, because we have not chosen a geometry.

```{r}
#| label: p1-layer1
ggplot(penguins, aes(x = bill_length_mm, y = bill_depth_mm))
```

## Layer 2: a geometry

```{r}
#| label: p1-layer2
ggplot(penguins, aes(x = bill_length_mm, y = bill_depth_mm)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE)
```

Overall, longer bills look shallower.

## Layer 3: map colour to species

```{r}
#| label: p1-layer3
ggplot(penguins, aes(x = bill_length_mm, y = bill_depth_mm, colour = species)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE)
```

Within each species, longer bills are deeper. The overall trend came from mixing three groups (Simpson's paradox).

## Mapping versus setting

Inside `aes()` a property is *mapped* to a variable. Outside `aes()` it is *set* to one fixed value.

```{r}
#| label: p1-setting
ggplot(penguins, aes(x = bill_length_mm, y = bill_depth_mm)) +
  geom_point(colour = "steelblue", size = 2, alpha = 0.6)
```

## Layer 4: labels and theme

```{r}
#| label: p1-layer4
p_bills <- ggplot(penguins, aes(x = bill_length_mm, y = bill_depth_mm, colour = species)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Within each species, longer bills are deeper",
       x = "Bill length (mm)",
       y = "Bill depth (mm)",
       colour = "Species") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

p_bills
```

## Save at a chosen size

```{r}
#| label: p1-save
ggsave("figures/bills.png", p_bills, width = 15, height = 10, units = "cm", dpi = 300)
```

# Practical 2: exploring data

Website chapters 2 to 4: *Distributions*, *Relationships* and *Change over time*.

## Distributions: histograms

Always choose the bin width.

```{r}
#| label: p2-histogram
ggplot(finches, aes(x = bdepth)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.25, fill = "grey60", colour = "white") +
  labs(x = "Beak depth (mm)", y = "Number of finches")
```

Lining up the groups in one column makes the shifts easy to see.

```{r}
#| label: p2-histogram-facets
#| fig-height: 6
ggplot(finches, aes(x = bdepth)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.25, fill = "grey60", colour = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~ group, ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = "Beak depth (mm)", y = "Number of finches")
```

## Distributions: box plot with the data

```{r}
#| label: p2-boxplot
ggplot(finches, aes(x = group, y = bdepth)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.5) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.5, colour = "#0072CF") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Beak depth (mm)")
```

## Distributions: show the data, not just the mean

```{r}
#| label: p2-mean-with-data
ggplot(penguins, aes(x = species, y = flipper_length_mm)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.3) +
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_se, colour = "#D6083B", size = 0.6) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Flipper length (mm)")
```

## Relationships: scatter plot and log scale

Income is skewed, so a log scale spreads out the crowded low values.

```{r}
#| label: p2-scatter
ggplot(gapminder, aes(x = income_per_person, y = life_expectancy)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_dollar(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Income per person (log scale)", y = "Life expectancy (years)")
```

## Relationships: small multiples with context

The first layer drops the region column, so every panel shows all countries in grey behind the highlighted region.

```{r}
#| label: p2-small-multiples
#| fig-height: 5.5
ggplot(gapminder, aes(x = income_per_person, y = life_expectancy)) +
  geom_point(data = select(gapminder, -region), colour = "grey85", size = 1.2) +
  geom_point(colour = "#0072CF", size = 1.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ region) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_dollar(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Income per person (log scale)", y = "Life expectancy (years)")
```

## Change over time: one line, then many

`group` draws one line per country.

```{r}
#| label: p2-lines
gap_years |>
  filter(country %in% c("Rwanda", "Brazil", "India", "United Kingdom")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = life_expectancy, colour = country)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Life expectancy (years)", colour = NULL)
```

Too many lines: highlight a few in context.

```{r}
#| label: p2-highlight-lines
focus <- gap_years |> filter(country %in% c("Rwanda", "Cambodia"))

ggplot(gap_years, aes(x = year, y = life_expectancy, group = country)) +
  geom_line(colour = "grey85") +
  geom_line(data = focus, aes(colour = country), linewidth = 1.2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Cambodia = "#EA7125", Rwanda = "#D6083B")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Life expectancy (years)", colour = NULL)
```

# Practical 3: designing for attention

Website chapters 5 to 7: *Ranking and ordering*, *Colour with purpose* and *Labels, titles and annotation*. The makeover below is the live coding sequence from the slides.

```{r}
#| label: p3-data
region_le <- gapminder |>
  group_by(region) |>
  summarise(life_expectancy = mean(life_expectancy))

region_le
```

## Makeover, before: the default

```{r}
#| label: p3-default
ggplot(region_le, aes(x = region, y = life_expectancy, fill = region)) +
  geom_col()
```

## Makeover step 1: sort and flip

```{r}
#| label: p3-sort
ggplot(region_le, aes(x = life_expectancy, y = fct_reorder(region, life_expectancy))) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(x = "Mean life expectancy (years)", y = NULL)
```

## Makeover step 2: grey and highlight

```{r}
#| label: p3-highlight
region_le |>
  mutate(focus = region == "Sub-Saharan Africa") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = life_expectancy, y = fct_reorder(region, life_expectancy), fill = focus)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey70", "#D6083B"), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Mean life expectancy (years)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

## Makeover step 3: headline and direct labels

```{r}
#| label: p3-final
p_makeover <- region_le |>
  mutate(focus = region == "Sub-Saharan Africa") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = life_expectancy, y = fct_reorder(region, life_expectancy), fill = focus)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", life_expectancy)),
            hjust = 1.2, colour = "white", fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey65", "#D6083B"), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
  labs(title = "Sub-Saharan Africa trails every other region by over 10 years",
       subtitle = "Mean life expectancy at birth across countries, 2010",
       caption = "Source: Gapminder", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        plot.title.position = "plot")

p_makeover
```

## Colour: a colour-blind safe palette

```{r}
#| label: p3-okabe-ito
species_cols <- c(Adelie = "#E69F00", Chinstrap = "#CC79A7", Gentoo = "#009E73")

ggplot(penguins, aes(x = bill_length_mm, y = flipper_length_mm, colour = species)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = species_cols) +
  labs(x = "Bill length (mm)", y = "Flipper length (mm)", colour = "Species")
```

## Colour: viridis for a continuous variable

```{r}
#| label: p3-viridis
ggplot(gapminder, aes(x = income_per_person, y = life_expectancy, colour = child_mortality)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_dollar(accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(direction = -1) +
  labs(x = "Income per person (log scale)", y = "Life expectancy (years)",
       colour = "Child deaths\nper 1,000")
```

## Labels: direct labels instead of a legend

```{r}
#| label: p3-direct-labels
region_years <- gap_years |>
  group_by(region, year) |>
  summarise(life_expectancy = mean(life_expectancy, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

line_ends <- region_years |> filter(year == max(year))

ggplot(region_years, aes(x = year, y = life_expectancy, colour = region)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_text(data = line_ends, aes(label = region),
            hjust = 0, nudge_x = 1.5, size = 3.6, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1960, 2010, 10),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.45))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean life expectancy (years)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

# Practical 4: finishing figures and the makeover challenge

Website chapters 8 to 10: *Honest scales and axes*, *Multi-panel figures and export* and *The makeover challenge*.

## Zoom without removing data

Scale limits throw data away before anything is calculated. `coord_cartesian()` only zooms the view.

```{r}
#| label: p4-zoom
base <- ggplot(penguins, aes(x = species, y = body_mass_g)) + geom_boxplot()

removed <- base + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(3000, 5000)) + ggtitle("Scale limits: data removed")
zoomed <- base + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(3000, 5000)) + ggtitle("Coordinate limits: zoomed")

removed | zoomed
```

## A multi-panel figure with panel letters

```{r}
#| label: p4-patchwork
#| fig-height: 6
p_hist <- ggplot(penguins, aes(x = flipper_length_mm)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 3, fill = "grey50", colour = "white") +
  labs(x = "Flipper length (mm)", y = "Count")

p_box <- ggplot(penguins, aes(x = species, y = body_mass_g)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Body mass (g)")

p_scatter <- ggplot(penguins, aes(x = bill_length_mm, y = bill_depth_mm, colour = species)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = species_cols) +
  labs(x = "Bill length (mm)", y = "Bill depth (mm)", colour = NULL)

p_panels <- (p_hist | p_box) / p_scatter + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")
p_panels
```

## Save at the final size

A single journal column is about 8.5 cm wide; a full page is about 17 cm. Save vector PDF for print and PNG for screens.

```{r}
#| label: p4-save
ggsave("figures/penguin_panels.pdf", p_panels, width = 17, height = 13, units = "cm")
ggsave("figures/makeover.png", p_makeover, width = 17, height = 9, units = "cm", dpi = 300)
```

## Makeover challenge: a worked example (brief 2)

**Brief:** show how body mass differs between species and between sexes, for a 30 second conference slide. Show the data, not just the means.

**Headline first:** *Gentoo penguins are the heaviest, and males outweigh females in every species.*

```{r}
#| label: p4-brief2
#| fig-height: 4.5
penguins |>
  drop_na(sex) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = species, y = body_mass_g, colour = sex)) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15, dodge.width = 0.6),
             alpha = 0.6, size = 1.8) +
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "crossbar", width = 0.5,
               position = position_dodge(width = 0.6), linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(female = "#CC79A7", male = "#0072B2")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(title = "Gentoo penguins are the heaviest,\nand males outweigh females in every species",
       x = NULL, y = "Body mass (g)", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Points: individual penguins. Bars: medians.") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", plot.title.position = "plot",
        plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())
```

Check it against the five questions: message, audience, chart, attention, integrity.
